venture.headline: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
venture.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.

venture.headline: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
venture.summary: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.

research.headline: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
research.summary: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware.

research.headline: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
research.summary: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment.

research.headline: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
research.summary: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt.

research.headline: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
research.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches.

research.headline: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
research.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,….

titans.headline: OpenAI Reaches $1.25 Trillion Valuation After Securing $11 Billion Funding Round
titans.summary: OpenAI secured $11 billion in a new funding round, raising its valuation to $1.25 trillion according to Bloomberg. This follows a March fundraising round where the company raised $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation. The latest capital injection positions OpenAI as one of the world's most valuable companies.

titans.headline: China reportedly recruited AI exec to spy on Jensen Huang
titans.summary: China's intelligence agency recruited Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to The New York Times. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) enlisted her to glean information about American AI chips and "potentially influence the company to push for its most advanced chips to be made available to China." Megaspeed […].

titans.headline: Meta’s Muse AI can create custom ‘spaces’ for the version of the app you need right now
titans.summary: Meta will now allow you to build customized, app-like experiences within Muse. The new feature, called "spaces," allows its AI assistant to build things like a shopping hub, school dashboard, music tracker, trivia game, and more, which you can interact with directly in the Muse app. Meta says you can create a new space by […].

titans.headline: Amazon will let you text Alexa your shopping list
titans.summary: Amazon is adding a new feature to Alexa for Shopping that allows customers to purchase items by texting the AI shopping assistant. Users can describe the products they're looking to buy and/or provide a photograph of the item, and Alexa for Shopping will search for matching results in Amazon listings, text back with recommendations, and […].

regulatory.headline: Progress Residential Will Pay $49.75 Million to Settle FTC Pricing Charges
regulatory.summary: Progress Residential and its owner Pretium Partners agreed to pay $49.75 million to settle Federal Trade Commission and state charges over deceptive rental pricing. The proposed order requires the companies to advertise true rental prices, disclose all fees clearly, and stop improperly withholding security deposits.

regulatory.headline: FTC and 22 States Detail Amazon's Alleged Search Ad Price-Inflation Scheme
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission and 22 states filed an updated complaint containing newly unredacted material about Amazon's advertising practices. The document details allegations that Amazon used deceptive and unfair methods to manipulate search ad auctions and secretly inflate prices to hit corporate financial targets.

regulatory.headline: FTC, Washington Take Action Against Payment Processor for Deceiving Small Businesses About Costs and Cancellation Terms
regulatory.summary: Riverside Payments falsely promised to save small businesses money on payment-processing services but failed to disclose fees and auto-renewing contracts, complaint alleges Payment processor Riverside Payments Inc., its affiliate Cascade Equipment Leasing LLC and their operators will pay $600,000 to resolve Federal Trade Commission and Washington state allegations that the firms deceived small businesses by falsely promising to save them money on payment processing services and making it nearly impossible to cancel despite offering “risk-free” cancellation.

voices.headline: A German Movie Previews Its Far-Right Future
voices.summary: The country’s cinema has recently taken a very dark turn.

macro.headline: Nvidia, AMD and other chip stocks rebound — but is relief from the ‘violent’ selloff only temporary?
macro.summary: Analysts warn of further volatility ahead, although there are several new factors that work in the AI trade’s favor.

frontier.headline: NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space
frontier.summary: After nearly 22 years of exploring the universe’s most violent explosions, NASA’s Swift Observatory has re-entered Earth’s atmosphere over Indonesia. Originally designed to last just two years, the pioneering space telescope transformed our understanding of black holes, exploding stars, and mysterious cosmic outbursts.

frontier.headline: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
frontier.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process.

frontier.headline: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
frontier.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations.

frontier.headline: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
frontier.summary: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap. We show that a ``blind'' preparation, designed from the clean chain without knowledge of the disorder realisation or its distribution, can start farther from stationarity yet overtake a reference in typical samples of a dephased disordered XX chain.

industry.headline: Horny Grandmas Are Having a Moment
industry.summary: Creators in their sixties, seventies, and eighties have flooded adult platforms as the demand for mature content has skyrocketed, with some turning to online sex work as a retirement lifeline.

industry.headline: Area Man Feels Joy Online for First Time in Years
industry.summary: A day after the US midterm elections gave Democrats control of Congress, Onion CEO Ben Collins and comedian Patti Harrison spoke to WIRED about the salve of satire during politically fraught times.

industry.headline: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished between Oakland and Texas
industry.summary: 6 pallets of hardware vanished en route to Texas, with no arrests 2 months later.

industry.headline: Developer ends lucrative screensaver deal with Roku because Fox bought it
industry.summary: Developer: “I can’t be part of the Fox world.”.

voices.headline: Governor Gavin Newsom Commutes 548 California Death-Row Sentences
voices.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans to commute all 548 state death-row sentences, reinforcing a nationwide trend of declining capital punishment. While 23 states have abolished the death penalty and executive commutations have grown, a small group of red states and the federal government continue to aggressively pursue executions. Consequently, outcomes for capital offenses are increasingly dictated by geographic boundaries.

voices.headline: Chuck Schumer’s Revenge
voices.summary: This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. This story was updated on November 5, 2026 at 11:00 am EST. Over the past two grim years, Chuck Schumer emerged as the symbol of everything that Democrats despised about themselves: the last aging Boomer who wouldn’t let go, the centrist without the steel to brawl with President Trump, a messenger forever mangling the message.

voices.headline: In Front of Their Noses
voices.summary: Truncheon-wielding, balaclava-wearing ICE agents did not swarm the polling stations. The Insurrection Act was not invoked, nor did the president order the 82nd Airborne to lock up Democratic officials. The men in leather trench coats did not slip out of black limousines at midnight to seize the editors of publications that are unfriendly to MAGA and all of its works.

voices.headline: Democrats Have No Coherent Plan for AI
voices.summary: Among the many gifts that Donald Trump bequeathed to Democrats ahead of the midterms was allowing them the exclusive political use of the AI backlash. Now that Democrats have decisively won control of Congress, voters will expect them to follow through on their rhetoric. The problem is that Democrats don’t actually have a plan to regulate AI.

voices.headline: The Pope Confronts One of His Toughest Political Challenges
voices.summary: Less than a month after losing part of a lung, Pope Leo XIV set out this morning on one of the longest and most ambitious trips of his pontificate. Over the course of 11 days and 12 flights, Leo will travel from South America’s Southern Cone to the high Andes and the Amazon Rainforest. Much of the Catholic world will be focused on how its 71-year-old leader, just a few weeks removed from cancer surgery, bears the physical challenge that the trip presents.
